headline: The proposal's headline claim — that you can cleave "hard physics" from a "flavour plugin layer" that "does not change molecular structure" — is culinary science that is simply wrong, and the document refutes itself in §7 (no sugar above 120°C; no oil in the bag; cut spices 30% in vacuum — three physical rules stated inside the flavour section). The correct cleavage is not physics-vs-flavour but **state variables / control variables (of which composition-with-a-timestamp is one) / outcome dimensions**; only the *identity of an aromatic* is a genuinely free plugin, because anything with a mass fraction has a physical consequence. That said, the owner is right and the first panel was defensive: the proposal has an **outcome vocabulary** and we have **none**. Our `itemPaths` returns paths named by mechanism (`'סו-ויד ← עישון'`) — a user who wants a texture must already know which machine produces it, and CP2 as specced will ship that same gap. Worse, we are blind to outcome levers **our own citations already hold**: `grz:'עקיף→ישיר'` and `grt`/`grh` are cited on 105 cuts and `itemStages` schedules every grill stage as a flat `hours:0.3` with no temperature and no zone; 23 cuts carry a numeric wrap trigger in `somid` ("עטיפה ב-75°C") that reaches the card as prose and never becomes a stage. And we have no collagen index at all — the single axis on which tenderness and chewiness both turn — we back-infer it from `c.doneness` being present and from one `tgt>=90` prose branch.

conceptsFound.concept: Separation of 'hard physics' (heat/moisture/time/place) from a 'flavour plugin layer' (rubs/marinades/sauces/glazes) that allegedly does not alter molecular structure — §1.1, §12
conceptsFound.steelman: Separating a transport/transformation model from a composition model is the enabling move for any parameter engine: it lets one master recipe generate many outcomes, and lets flavour be swapped without recomputing safety. As a *dependency-direction* claim (physics never depends on which chilli you chose) it is correct and valuable.
conceptsFound.value: Adopt the dependency direction, reject the membrane. The cleavage leaks in six named places, each of which a pitmaster lives inside: (1) SALT — dissolves myosin, raises water-holding capacity, depresses surface water activity (so it governs pellicle, smoke adhesion and bark set), and over 24-48h at 68°C in a bag produces a cured/hammy texture; our own MAKES `calc.salt` is already a g/kg NUMBER because we already know salt is physics. (2) SUGAR — a Maillard/caramelisation accelerant with a per-sugar onset (fructose ~110°C, sucrose ~160°C, maltose ~180°C) and a humectant that sets bark; the doc's own Rule 3 and §7 treat it as physics. (3) ACID — denatures surface protein, moves pH across the isoelectric point (~5.2) where water-holding is MINIMISED, and retards Maillard, so it moves crispness and colour directly. (4) SURFACE FAT — the conduction/radiation coupling medium; blocks evaporative cooling; and in a vacuum bag actively harmful. (5) WRAP — one binary that moves four dimensions at once: ends evaporative cooling (ends the stall), softens bark (foil) or preserves it (paper), terminates smoke uptake, accelerates conduction if liquid is added. (6) SMOKE — a flavour whose intensity is a function of physical state (surface moisture, combustion completeness, meat below ~60-65°C for the ring). Correct model: every treatment is `{what, when, howMuch}`; only `what` at the aromatic level is free. Salt at T-24h is a physics move; salt at T-0 is a flavour move.

conceptsFound.concept: PREFERENCE_TEXTURE / PREFERENCE_FLAVOR as ENGINE INPUTS that route to a PROCESS_FLOW — §2.3, §3.2 — surfaced as §8's three plain-language buttons ('fast' / 'crisp and traditional' / 'extra tender and juicy')
conceptsFound.steelman: The user states the DESIRED OUTCOME in the language of eating, and the engine derives the machine sequence. Path selection becomes a consequence of intent rather than a piece of expert knowledge the user must already possess. Done well, the same three cited paths we already enumerate get relabelled by what they produce, and the mechanism name becomes a detail.
conceptsFound.value: This is the single biggest gap on this lens and I will not hedge it. `itemPaths(meta)` (app.js:4175) returns `{id, methodKey, order, label}` where label is `comboMethodEntry`'s mechanism string ('סו-ויד + עישון') or `svOrderName`'s ('עישון ← סו-ויד'). `SV_SMOKE_ORDERS[].desc` carries outcome PROSE ('flavor and crust', 'maximal smoke ring') but it is unwired (the code comment at app.js:3826 says so) and is prose, not a dimension. CP2's approved path panel will ship the same mechanism-named list. Fixing it costs no new safety data: it is a relabelling of paths we already cite, driven by an outcome vector we can compute from fields we mostly already have.

conceptsFound.concept: `collagen_level: HIGH | LOW` as a first-class intrinsic property of the cut — §4.5 MeatInput, Rule 1
conceptsFound.steelman: Connective-tissue density is THE axis on which both tenderness and chewiness turn, and it decides which of two opposite prescriptions applies. Declared per cut, it makes 'how tender do you want it' a meaningful question and makes an impossible request detectable.
conceptsFound.value: We have an UNDECLARED, UNCITED collagen model hiding in two places: `methodRules(c)` (app.js:989) branches on `c.doneness` being present ('steak-like') versus falling through to 'collagen/long cuts', and app.js:1589 branches on `c.tgt>=90` to advise a long cambro hold. Neither is named, neither is cited, neither is queryable. Tenderness is a two-term function with OPPOSITE SIGNS — `w_c·collagenConverted(T,t) − w_m·fibreContraction(T_peak)`, with w_c ~ collagen density — so a single tenderness slider is meaningless until the engine knows the regime. Proposed field `collagen: 0|1|2|3` (0 = tenderloin, 3 = shank/cheek). Highest value per byte of anything on my list.

conceptsFound.concept: Per-stage ADVANCE CONDITIONS on internal temperature, not duration — `TRIGGER_NEXT_STAGE_WHEN = (TIME_ELAPSED == 2_HOURS) OR (P_TARGET_INT == 50°C)`; 'wrap at 71°C' (§3.2, §4.5, §6.3)
conceptsFound.steelman: Every outcome dimension worth naming is a time-at-temperature INTEGRAL, and the stall is an evaporative plateau at a temperature, not on a clock. A stage that can only say 'how long' cannot express when collagen conversion starts, when fat render begins, when smoke uptake ends, or when to wrap.
conceptsFound.value: Confirmed independently and I rank it #1 with the outcome vocabulary. `itemStages` (app.js:4093) emits stages carrying `hours` and, only at the very end, one `kind:'bcheck'` temperature gate. Meanwhile 23 cuts carry a NUMERIC wrap trigger in `somid` — 17× 'עטיפה ב-75°C', 5× 'עטיפה ב-70°C', 1× 'עטיפה ב-65°C' — which reaches the recipe card as a prose step (app.js:1586) and NEVER becomes a stage, a task, or a timeline event. We already hold the data for the doc's flagship example and throw it away at the stage boundary. Proposed: `advanceWhen:{coreC?, surfaceC?, hours?, mode:'first'|'all'}` plus a real `wrap:{at:{coreC}, material, reason}` stage kind.

conceptsFound.concept: Rule 1 — CHEWINESS PROTECTION as the FIRST hard rule (§4.1)
conceptsFound.steelman: The engine's first duty is to stop you making something unpleasant to chew. Naming chewiness as its own outcome, ahead of safety in the rule list, is a correct product instinct: it is what users actually complain about.
conceptsFound.value: The doc names the concept and implements exactly one cause. Chewiness has FOUR causes with CONTRADICTORY remedies, and the engine's real value is saying WHICH: C1 under-converted collagen (rubbery — fix: more T×t); C2 over-contracted fibre past actin denaturation ~66°C (dry and stringy — fix: LESS heat, the opposite prescription); C3 skin/casing/membrane leather (fix: neither — a prep action or a dehydrating finish); C4 sliced WITH the grain (fix: a serving instruction). We already hold all four in prose in the troubleshooting table — app.js:4753 (dry is usually UNDER-cooked), 4756 ('גומי' = under-converted collagen), 4757 (crumbly = over-converted), 4767 ('העור לעיס' = pellicle/casing soak) — and jerky's `note` says 'לפרוס 5 מ״מ נגד הסיבים'. This is a REPRESENTATION conversion, not new research: turn a prose lookup into a derived `chew:{risk, cause}`.

conceptsFound.concept: Glaze mechanism (§4.2) — sugar-based glaze delayed to the last 15-30 min, and only under dry heat; sauce removed from a sous-vide bag and reduced separately
conceptsFound.steelman: Glaze timing is a computable burn-budget problem, not a rule of thumb. Surface temperature sits between wet-bulb and chamber temp depending on wetness, so a glaze is protected while wet and starts burning the moment it sets — which is the real mechanism behind thin layered coats, each coat resetting evaporative protection.
conceptsFound.value: We already SCHEDULE this and the doc only describes it: app.js:7273 emits a clock-bound glaze task at `lastCook.end − 15min`, and the mise-en-place clusterer deliberately excludes it (`// glaze stays clock-bound!`). But ours is a CONSTANT — blind to sugar type and to the final chamber temperature. A honey glaze (fructose, ~110°C onset) on a 230°C grill finish and a maple glaze on a 110°C smoke finish get the same 15 minutes. Proposed: `glazeStartOffset = f(lowest caramelisation temp of the sugar, final-stage chamber T, number of coats, humidity)` with a guard when chamberT exceeds the burn ceiling. Also missing on both sides: a glaze IS a rehumidification event, so max bark crispness and a heavy glaze are mutually exclusive and the engine should say so.

conceptsFound.concept: Smoke-intensity coefficient per device class (§4.3: offset 1.5, charcoal cabinet 1.2, pellet 0.8, electric/gas 0.6) returned as `smoke_intensity_multiplier`
conceptsFound.steelman: Smoke intensity is a device-and-fuel property multiplied by exposure while the surface is still receptive. Making it a number lets the engine warn ('your pellet grill will give a mild smoke on this cut — extend the early window or add a smoke tube') instead of printing the same wood name to everyone.
conceptsFound.value: We have zero smoke modelling: `c.wood` is prose ('אלון/היקורי'), matched against `cap.loadedWood` free text (app.js:7252) by substring, and the smoker device has no smoke term at all. Adopt the SHAPE, cite our own numbers, and crucially multiply by a TIME WINDOW rather than the whole cook: smoke uptake is heavily front-loaded (moist surface, cool meat), which is why the doc's own disaster-recovery narrative correctly says 'the meat has already absorbed the smoke it needs'. Also missing from both: combustion quality (clean blue vs dirty white smoke) — the #1 real-world cause of bitter BBQ.

conceptsFound.steelman: A gain/loss vector per route is exactly the right shape for choosing among routes: it turns 'which path' from a mechanism question into a trade-off the user can actually make.
conceptsFound.value: Better than the doc's own version: attach the deltas PER STAGE, not per conversion, so they compose. Then `deltas:[{dim:'crisp', sign:-1, why:'foil wrap'}, {dim:'smoke', sign:-1, why:'wrapped at 75°C'}]` falls out of the plan automatically instead of being a hand-authored table per method pair, and it feeds CP2's path panel directly.

conceptsFound.concept: The MASTER RECIPE thesis (§1.1) — do not store 100 brisket recipes; store one parameterised recipe. Corollary the owner raises: a parameter engine should let each catalog card hold LESS.
conceptsFound.steelman: If most of what distinguishes two recipes is a combination of the same variables, the variables belong in the engine and the card should carry only what is irreducibly specific to that cut.
conceptsFound.value: We already have the master recipe: `itemProfile`→`validCombo`→`comboMethodEntry`→`itemStages` GENERATE every stage and every combination from a parameter record. But on this lens the shrink comes from the opposite direction than the doc thinks. The numbers cannot shrink (they are cited facts, and 89% of `(svt,svh,smt,smh,tgt,safe)` tuples are distinct). What CAN shrink is the ~20% hand-written PROSE body — because most of it is outcome explanation and remedy that a proper outcome vocabulary would DERIVE: the troubleshooting table, the treatment texts (`treatText`/`soTreatText`), the `somid`/`mid`/`sear` free-text (25 distinct `sear` strings, 30 distinct `somid` strings today), and the per-path descriptions. Structure the outcome model and that prose becomes generated, translatable ordinals and codes.

conceptsFound.concept: Equipment-gated cookability — Rule 5 (cheese <30°C), §4.3 `Validate_Equipment_For_Cut`, §4.5 blocking checks, §11 scenario B ('your oven and grill run too hot; here is what to buy')
conceptsFound.steelman: Correlating what can be cooked, and how, against the kit the user actually owns, and refusing with a reason and a purchasable fix, is the right product behaviour.
conceptsFound.value: Ours is structurally stronger and I will say it plainly. `eqmValidity(meta)` (app.js:1859) runs ownership over EVERY cited path, returns `{level:'ok'|'blocked-default'|'uncookable', okPaths, gaps, fixes}`, distinguishes 'the default combo fails but another cited path works' from 'nothing works' (so it never cries wolf), separates device-kind gaps from probe gaps, and emits gaps as CODES (`{kind:'smoker', state:'missing'}`) with the sentence built only at render. The doc `throw`s a Hebrew string from business logic. One genuine hole the doc exposes on my lens: our smoker device has `maxC` as a FLOOR check only (equipment.js:162 — the device must REACH the cited temp), so there is no way to express a CEILING requirement, and cold smoking (cheese, cold-smoked fish, gravlax) is a ceiling constraint. Add a cold-smoke generator token and a max-temp-ceiling capability.

conceptsFound.concept: Rules 2/4/7 — poultry pasteurisation as temperature×time; and silent target rewriting (`SET P_TARGET_INT = 52°C`, `SET P_TARGET_INT = 63°C`)
conceptsFound.steelman: Pasteurisation as a temperature×time function rather than a threshold is correct food science and is the intellectual basis of sous-vide.
conceptsFound.value: The principle is ours already and better: our `sources.py` reasons on THICKNESS (chicken breast: '0.4kg is ~30-40mm, Baldwin requires 65°C/30mm = 1h15'), which is Baldwin's actual third axis and which the doc lacks entirely. Reject the mechanism: an engine that silently rewrites a user's target is the one thing this engine must never do. Keep as a written invariant — a rule may ADD a stage, CHOOSE among cited paths, or SHIFT a stage's position; it may never author a temperature.

conceptsFound.concept: §8's four-step flow: raw material → flavour profile (filtered to what suits the cut) → outcome path → dashboard
conceptsFound.steelman: Ordering matters: choosing flavour BEFORE the outcome path is right, because the flavour choice constrains the physics (a sugar rub imposes a burn ceiling, which forbids a 250°C finish). Filtering flavour profiles to the ones that suit the protein removes a whole class of bad choices before they are made.
conceptsFound.value: We filter seasonings by `cats` (a per-seasoning category list) so the filtering half exists. The ORDERING is wrong for us: seasoning is chosen late and independently of the path, so the sugar-rub → burn-ceiling → finish-temp coupling can never be enforced. And our seasoning composition is not machine-readable in the way this needs: `SEASONING_TAGS` gives `{flavor:[...], base:'יבש'|'רטוב', heat:0-3}` — `heat` is CHILLI heat, and sweetness is only the flavour word 'מתוק'. There is no sugar mass fraction and no sugar TYPE, so the burn ceiling cannot be computed. A `sugar:{type, level}` and `acid:{level}` on ~289 seasonings is the cheapest enabling change here.

conceptsFound.concept: Faux Cambro / insulated-cooler hold as a scheduling BUFFER (§5.4, §5.5 processTelemetry TRANSFER_TO_COOLER)
conceptsFound.steelman: An item finished early can be parked hot, freeing grate space and de-stressing the timeline. A holding vessel is a genuine optimisation resource, not just a container.
conceptsFound.value: We have the `cooler` equipment token (equipment_map.py, attached when smoke hours ≥4 or rest ≥30) and Phase 3a plans a cook-early-and-hold move with a 60°C floor, a 240-min danger-zone accumulator and a 360-min `holdCapMin`. But those are all SAFETY caps. On my lens there is a missing QUALITY cap, and it is per-cut and much shorter: a hot hold keeps losing moisture, so a brisket holds beautifully for 4 hours while a lean pork loin is ruined in 45 minutes. And crispness has a SHELF LIFE measured in minutes — a crisped skin put in a cambro is destroyed. Cook-early-and-hold is in direct conflict with `prikhut ≥ 2` and somebody has to price that conflict before Phase 3a ships.

conceptsFound.concept: Method-conversion engine with time factors (§4.4: SMOKE→PRESSURE 0.12, SMOKE→SOUS_VIDE 2.5) and §11 scenario C (chicken liver grill→sous-vide, 5 min → 45 min, warns 'no crust')
conceptsFound.steelman: Answering 'what if I did this the other way' with a re-timed plan plus an explicit statement of what is gained and lost is a genuinely useful feature and the right way to present alternatives.
conceptsFound.value: Adopt the OUTPUT (a re-timed alternative with an explicit gain/loss vector), reject the MULTIPLIER. Sous-vide duration is a pasteurisation value — temperature × time × thickness — so generating it by multiplication is exactly the forbidden move. Our equivalent is `itemPaths` enumerating cited combos with cited schedules per path, which is the safe version of the same feature; what it lacks is the gain/loss vector, i.e. concept #8.

conceptsFound.concept: P_MOIST_ENV as an explicit control variable: DRY | WET | VACUUM (§3.1)
conceptsFound.steelman: Naming the moisture environment as a first-class control is correct and underrated — it is what determines whether a crust can form at all, because a wet surface is pinned near the wet-bulb temperature and cannot brown.
conceptsFound.value: We model humidity only obliquely: `waterPan` as a smoker device prop (never required by any recipe), `rh_pct:(70,80)` on cure-chamber specials, and `drySurfaceHours(svHours)=clamp(svHours*0.3, 0.25, 4)` as our one real surface-drying model. A declared `moisture: dry|humid|wet|vacuum` per stage is what makes the crispness prediction computable at all, and it is what lets `waterPan` finally mean something.

whereItBeatsUs:
Four places, stated without hedging.

**1. It has an outcome vocabulary; we have none.** `itemPaths(meta)` (app.js:4175) returns paths labelled by mechanism — `comboMethodEntry`'s `'סו-ויד + עישון'` (app.js:3782) or `svOrderName`'s `'עישון ← סו-ויד'` (app.js:3833). To choose a texture our user must already know which machine produces it. The proposal's §8 asks in the language of eating. `SV_SMOKE_ORDERS[].desc` does carry outcome prose ('flavor and crust', 'maximal smoke ring') but the code's own comment at app.js:3826 records that it is DEAD — never rendered. CP2's approved path panel is specced to select among cited paths and will ship the identical gap.

**2. It declares `collagen_level`; we hide ours.** `methodRules(c)` (app.js:989) decides the whole texture regime by testing whether `c.doneness` exists, falling through to a comment that says 'collagen/long cuts'. app.js:1589 uses `c.tgt>=90` for the same purpose in a different place. That is an undeclared, uncited, duplicated model of the single most important culinary property in the catalog. Tenderness is `w_c·collagenConverted(T,t) − w_m·fibreContraction(T_peak)` with the two terms opposite in sign and `w_c` set by collagen density — without the field, no tenderness or chewiness prediction is possible at all.

**3. Its stages advance on internal temperature; ours only on the clock.** `itemStages` (app.js:4093) emits `hours` per stage plus one terminal `kind:'bcheck'`. We have 23 cuts whose `somid` carries an explicit numeric wrap trigger (17× 'עטיפה ב-75°C', 5× 'עטיפה ב-70°C', 1× 'עטיפה ב-65°C'); it reaches the card as a prose step at app.js:1586 and never becomes a stage, a task or a timeline event. The stall is an evaporative plateau at a temperature; every outcome dimension is a time-at-temperature integral; a schedule that knows only durations cannot integrate.

**4. It has a smoke-intensity number; we have a string.** Its device coefficients (offset 1.5 / cabinet 1.2 / pellet 0.8 / electric 0.6) are directionally right. Our `c.wood` is prose matched by substring against `cap.loadedWood` free text (app.js:7252), and the smoker device carries no smoke term whatsoever.

**And two self-inflicted wounds the comparison exposed, where our OWN citations are orphaned.** `sources.py` carries `grt` (grill temp), `grh` (grill hours) and `grz` (zone strategy, e.g. `'עקיף→ישיר'`) on **105 of 130 cuts**; `app.js` reads them at lines 2825-2826 and 2897 for a stat cell and a tooltip only. `comboMethodEntry` does `if(combo.includes('grill')) hours+=0.3;` and `itemStages` pushes `hours:0.3` with no temp and no zone. A picanha whose cited grill schedule is 230°C / 0.75 h indirect→direct is scheduled as 18 minutes of undifferentiated 'גריל / אש ישירה'. `grz` is the two-zone reverse-sear — the single most important crispness-versus-gradient lever in grilling — and our grill device already declares `zones` as its capacity key (app.js EQUIP_CATS). We have the data and the capability and join neither. Separately, `grillable` is cited on all 130 cuts (25 False) but `methodRules` uses category heuristics instead; I measured 3 live disagreements where the citation says no and the heuristic allows grill-only (#74 כבד אווז, #80 מוח עגל, #102 שום שלם מעושן).
whereWeAreBetter:
Seven, each verified in code and each defensible on culinary grounds rather than on process.

**1. Two cited schedules per cut for the same texture goal.** We ship `svt/svh` (combo path) and `sot/soh` (smoke-only) plus separate cited `order_svsmoke` and `order_smokesv` blocks with their own `cold` and `pasteurize` flags. That is a measured two-point sample of the collagen-conversion curve per cut: brisket 68°/30h, beef cheek 80°/24h, ox-tail 79°/24-48h, tongue 70°/24-48h. The doc emits two constants — `68°C, 24_HOURS` for every HIGH-collagen cut and `71°C`/`74°C` targets by category. Culinarily those are four different textures collapsed into one.

**2. Per-cut doneness as a real outcome parameter.** `doneness.levels` with per-level °C and a per-cut `scale` (`steak`/`dark`/`white`), on 23 cuts, read by `donenessTarget`/`currentDoneness`/`doneLabel`. That IS a parameter engine on the one outcome dimension we implemented, and it is finer-grained than the doc's `P_TARGET_INT` free number.

**3. Structured composition where composition is physics.** `MAKES[].build.calc = {salt:18, cure, cureRate:2.5, sugar, water:10, brine}` — grams per kilo, with cure type and rate, which is exactly the salt-as-physics model the doc's own §1.1 denies. The doc's `FlavorProfile` is `{rub_type:'DRY'|'NONE', has_sugar:boolean}` and `has_sugar` is never read.

**4. The cook-ORDER question is cited, not asserted.** `comboHasSvSmoke` requires `order_smokesv.sv.pasteurize === true` before the reverse order is offered at all, and `itemStages` reads `osm.cold` per item rather than assuming (the BUG-1 comment records exactly this correction). The doc's §3.2 flagship — smoke to 50°C core, chill, vacuum, hold 24h at 68°C — is reduced-oxygen packaging with no cooling rate, no danger-zone budget and no nitrite. We gate that specific manoeuvre on a citation.

**5. Glaze is already scheduled, not merely described.** app.js:7273 places the glaze task at `lastCook.end − 15min` and the mise-en-place clusterer explicitly refuses to batch it (`// glaze stays clock-bound!`). The doc describes glaze timing in prose in §4.2 and its own §4.5 code emits it as a fixed 15-minute pipeline stage with no relation to the preceding stage's end.

**6. Refusals are codes with an ordered fix ladder.** `eqmValidity` returns `{level, okPaths, gaps:[{kind,state}], fixes:[configure|switch-path|replace]}` and distinguishes 'blocked-default' from 'uncookable' precisely so it does not cry wolf on an item cookable another cited way. The doc `throw`s interpolated Hebrew from business logic.

**7. The chewiness knowledge already exists — in the wrong representation.** app.js:4753-4767 already encodes the C1/C2/C3 split correctly and unusually well: 'dry meat is usually UNDER-cooked, not over'; 'rubbery = under-converted collagen, needs 90-96°C internal, far past steak doneness'; 'crumbly = over-converted'; 'leathery casing = under-soaked natural casing or too-thick pellicle'. That is better pitmaster knowledge than anything in the proposal. It is trapped in a prose lookup table instead of being a derived outcome — which makes the fix a conversion job, not a research job.
proposedModel:
**The vocabulary I would actually want us to implement.** Five layers. Nothing here authors a safety number; preferences select among cited paths and shift stage positions only.

**A. Cut intrinsics — 6 new cited fields on CUTS (the missing physics substrate).**
- `collagen: 0|1|2|3` — connective-tissue index (0 tenderloin → 3 shank/cheek/brisket-flat). Replaces the hidden `c.doneness ? steak : collagen` test in `methodRules` and the `tgt>=90` test at app.js:1589. Highest value of anything on this list.
- `fatIntra: 0|1|2|3` — intramuscular fat. Drives render axis and forgiveness of overshoot.
- `fatSub: 'none'|'thin'|'cap'|'skin'` — drives the crispness path, the scoring requirement, and fat-side-up/down.
- `thickMm: number` — the axis Baldwin actually indexes on and which our own `sources.py` note for chicken breast already reasons about ('~30-40mm → 65°C/30mm = 1h15'). `kg` is not thickness. Seed from `shape`+`kg` (we already have `SHAPE_CM2_PER_KG` classes: slab/roast/pieces/bird/long) and mark `derived` until cited. Determines come-up time, pasteurisation, the overcooked band, and the crisp-versus-interior race.
- `fibre: 'fine'|'medium'|'coarse'` + `grainKnown: boolean` — drives chewiness cause C4 and the slicing instruction.
- `skin: 'none'|'thin'|'thick'|'casing'` — drives chewiness cause C3.

**B. User preference inputs — FOUR sliders plus two enums, plain Hebrew, sane defaults.** This is §8 executed properly.
- `mrkam` 0-3 (`שמור נגיסה ↔ נימוח מתפרק`) — **bounded per cut by `collagen`**: a fillet cannot offer 'מתפרק' and the UI must say why rather than offer it.
- `prikhut` 0-3 (`רך ↔ פריך מאוד`).
- `ashan` 0-3 (`עדין ↔ עז`).
- `zmanBudget` — a CONSTRAINT, not a texture word. This is what actually distinguishes the doc's 'fast' button from its 'traditional' button.
- `glaze: 'none'|'light'|'heavy'`, `sauce: 'none'|'side'|'onTop'`.

**C. New stage fields on `itemStages` output.**
- `advanceWhen: {coreC?, surfaceC?, hours?, mode:'first'|'all'}`.
- `wrap: {at:{coreC}, material:'paper'|'foil'|null, reason:'stall'|'speed'|'moisture'}` — a REAL stage kind, sourced from the 23 numeric triggers already sitting in `somid`.
- `zone: 'indirect'|'direct'|'twoZone'` ← the orphaned `grz`.
- `tempC` and `hours` on the grill stage ← the orphaned `grt`/`grh` on 105 cuts, replacing the flat `hours:0.3`.
- `moisture: 'dry'|'humid'|'wet'|'vacuum'` — the doc's `P_MOIST_ENV`, which is what makes crispness computable and what finally gives `waterPan` a consumer.
- `surfaceTargetC` on a finish stage — the crispness gate.
- `serveWithinMin` on the last stage when `prikhut>=2` — crispness has a shelf life and the scheduler must honour it.

**D. The predicted outcome vector — computed PER PATH, which is what makes CP2 an outcome panel instead of a mechanism list.**
```
outcome = {
  tenderness: 0-3,
  chew: { risk: 0-3, cause: 'collagen'|'fibre'|'skin'|'grain'|null },
  crisp: 0-3, juiciness: 0-3, smoke: 0-3, fatRender: 0-3, colour: 0-3,
  confidence: 'cited'|'derived',
  deltas: [ {dim:'crisp', sign:-1, why:'wrap.foil'}, {dim:'smoke', sign:-1, why:'wrap@75C'} ]
}
```
Dependencies, stated as the actual physics:
- `tenderness ≈ w_c·collagenConverted(∫k(T)dt, k≈Arrhenius, ~0 below 55°C, meaningful from 68°C, fast above 85°C) − w_m·fibreContraction(T_peak vs actin ~66°C)`, `w_c = collagen/3`. Add a third term for **proteolysis** (cathepsins active to ~55-60°C) which is why 55°C/48h short rib is a genuinely different texture from 68°C/30h — we ship both temps and never say they differ.
- `crisp ≈ f(surface a_w at start of finish [<~0.4-0.5 needed], ∫(surfaceT−150°C)⁺dt, fatRenderedFraction, surfacePH, wrap material) × decay(timeSinceFinish, covered?)`. Until the surface is dry it is pinned near 100°C by evaporation and cannot brown — this is why `drySurfaceHours` is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
- `chew.risk = max(C1 collagen high AND converted<thr, C2 lean AND T_peak>fibreContractionT, C3 skin/casing AND no dehydrating finish, C4 coarse fibre AND grain not asserted)`; **report the cause**, because the four remedies contradict each other.
- `glazeStartOffset = coats × timeToSet(coatThickness, finalChamberT, RH)`, guarded by `burnCeiling(sugarType)` — fructose/honey ~110°C, glucose ~150°C, sucrose ~160°C, maltose ~180°C.
- `smoke ≈ deviceCoef × ∫(exposure while surface moist AND core<~65°C) × surfaceArea/mass × (1 − wrapped)`; smoke-ring formation is impossible once core passes ~60-65°C — which is the physical justification for the `order_smokesv` school we already cite.
- `juiciness ≈ waterRetained(T_peak, salt, cookRate) + gelatinHeld + fatRetained − holdLoss(holdMin, holdC)`.

**E. Outcome guards — a visibly DIFFERENT class from safety guards, emitted as `{code, params}` only** (the `eqmValidity.gaps` precedent; never prose from the engine):
`CRISP_VS_FOIL`, `CRISP_VS_SAUCE_ON_TOP`, `CRISP_VS_HOLD` (direct conflict with Phase-3a cook-early-and-hold), `GLAZE_BURN_CEILING`, `TENDER_IMPOSSIBLE_NO_COLLAGEN` (not discouraged — impossible: 'this cut has no connective tissue to melt; long cooking will only dry it'), `CHEW_RISK_<cause>`, `SLICE_AGAINST_GRAIN_REQUIRED`.

**F. Two enabling data changes outside CUTS.** (i) `sugar:{type, level}` and `acid:{level}` on the ~289 seasonings — today `SEASONING_TAGS` gives only `{flavor, base, heat}` where `heat` is chilli heat, so the burn ceiling is uncomputable. (ii) A cold-smoke generator token plus a max-temp **CEILING** capability — `eqmSatisfies` today only floors `cap.maxTempC` ('device must REACH the cited temp', equipment.js:162), so cold smoking cannot be expressed as a requirement at all.

**G. The invariant, written and tested:** a preference or rule may ADD a stage, CHOOSE among cited paths, or SHIFT a stage's position; it may never author or rewrite `safe`, `svt/svh`, `smt/smh`, `sot/soh` or `tgt`. Every number stays cited; the engine only ever decides *which* cited number applies and *when*.
openQuestions: Are the six new cut intrinsics (collagen, fatIntra, fatSub, thickMm, fibre, skin) citable at our standard, or must they ship as `derived` with a visible confidence flag? `collagen` is arguably an anatomical fact rather than a safety value — does it face the same evidential bar as `safe`, or a lower one? This decides whether the whole model is a data-research project or a weekend of annotation.

Is `thickMm` derivable from `shape`+`kg` accurately enough for Baldwin-grade pasteurisation reasoning, or must it be cited per cut? Our own chicken-breast source note reasons on 30-40mm, so the accuracy bar is real, not decorative.

Crispness has a shelf life of minutes and it directly contradicts Phase-3a's cook-early-and-hold move. Does the crisp constraint get to VETO an orchestrator hold, or only warn? And what is the per-cut QUALITY hold cap (distinct from the 360-min safety `holdCapMin`) — brisket 4h versus lean loin 45min is a >5x spread that nothing currently prices.

Do the outcome preferences persist per-recipe (adopting the existing `mk-item-path` key pattern) or per-user as a default profile? The doc implies a per-user equipment-and-taste profile; our PREFS registry design implies per-key.

Should the outcome vector be shown always, or only when the user opens the path panel? Showing predicted `crisp/chew/juiciness` on every catalog card is a large claim surface — and the ordinals are translation-cheap (they are codes, not prose) which argues for showing more, not less.

Reversing the flow order so seasoning is chosen BEFORE the path (so a sugar rub can impose a burn ceiling on the finish temperature) is a real UX change to a shipped flow. Is that in scope, or does the coupling get enforced as a late-stage guard instead?

`grz`/`grt`/`grh` are cited on 105 cuts and orphaned; `grillable` is cited on all 130 and overridden by category heuristics in 3 measured cases. Do we fix those as a standalone correctness task now (they are pure wiring against existing citations), or hold them until the outcome model lands so the grill stage is redesigned once rather than twice?
